doc.title: Scott Jimmy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Contracts, no lawyers and Savoy's reputation
summary: He had no lawyer or manager and learned the contract too late; lawyers avoided Lubinsky.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Yet, in that period in the 1950s, you recorded a number of songs . . .

. . . that you’re proud of and that got through even though you weren’t in charge of the recording and you weren’t really asked what you wanted to record. But nonetheless, aren’t there a lot of those recordings that you love and that you like?
Some, but I wasn’t big on them, because I couldn’t do my own selection of the tunes.
So you continue to be frustrated by your ability to choose the material . . .
. . . that was most close to your heart.

You go through it, because he throws in your mind about he owns you and the contract he’s got on you. You don’t know how they negotiate those contracts and things. You don’t know, because I never did know just what it was, and when I found out, it was too late.
Too late, because you were contractually obligated. You had no legal advice at that time? You had no lawyer?

No. I had no legal contact or person that would work for me. It was because of him. They knew him so well. Lawyers and everything knew him so well, they didn’t want to be bothered. If you were related with him . . .
I’m not going to give you any legal advice, because I don’t want to mess with him.
They didn’t want to handle – do anything for any of the artists that he was handling. That’s why I say, poor Maybelle. I know she had a rough time with . . .
